draft.title: Dijkstra's algorithm
card: Dijkstra's algorithm finds the shortest path from one start vertex to every other vertex in a weighted network. The start gets the label 0. Every other vertex starts with no label.
Each step, fix the unvisited vertex with the smallest label. Then look at its neighbours. New label = fixed label + edge weight. Keep the new label only if it is smaller than the old one.
Edges are A-B 4, A-C 2, C-B 1, B-D 5 and C-D 8. Start at A. Fix C (2). B drops from 4 to 3 via C, and D gets 10. Fix B (3). D drops to 8. Fix D (8).
The shortest distance from A to D is 8. Trace back through the labels to find the path: A-C-B-D.
draft.remember: Fix the smallest label, update its neighbours, and keep only smaller labels.

a.q: After the start is fixed, the unvisited vertices have labels B 6, C 3 and D 9. Which vertex is fixed next?
opts: C, as it has the smallest label
D, as it has the largest label
B, as it comes next after A in order
D, as it is furthest from the start
a.why: The algorithm always fixes the unvisited vertex with the smallest label, so C is fixed. Choosing B because of its place in the alphabet ignores the labels, which is what the method is based on.
a.clue: Look at the numbers, not the letters.

b.q: Four towns are joined by roads (in km): P-Q 7, P-R 3, R-Q 2, Q-S 4 and R-S 9. Using Dijkstra's algorithm from P, what is the shortest distance from P to S?
opts: 9 km
11 km
12 km
5 km
b.why: Fix P (0). Then R gets 3 and Q gets 7. Fix R (3): Q drops to 5 via R, and S gets 12. Fix Q (5): S drops to 9. The path P-R-Q-S is 3 + 2 + 4 = 9. The 11 km answer comes from P-Q-S, which uses the first label for Q and misses the cheaper route through R.
b.clue: Check whether going through R makes Q closer.

a.best: C, as it has the smallest label
